reason: I'll start with the fibroblast branch to work toward the supporting tissue goal.
expectation: I expect the timed conditions to guide descendants toward fibroblasts, though there may be intermediate stages.

effect: The fibroblast branch activates collagen genes and produces RNA messages, so I can now follow those messages into protein production.
reaction: The unchanged DNA alongside selective gene activity makes the differentiation connection clear.
reason: Combine the collagen-message cells with amino acids to progress toward supporting tissue.
expectation: I expect ribosomes to use the messages and amino acids to make collagen or a collagen precursor.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch also needs attention, but I want to continue the fibroblast sequence first.

effect: The cells make procollagen in the ER and Golgi, ready for secretion rather than already having extracellular collagen.
reaction: The distinction between a precursor in vesicles and finished tissue is useful.
reason: Use the extracellular fluid to continue building the supporting tissue.
expectation: I expect procollagen to be secreted and processed outside the fibroblasts, possibly forming collagen fibers.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch remains a goal, but I prefer to continue the collagen sequence first.

effect: The procollagen is secreted and assembled into extracellular collagen fibres; combining the matrix with living fibroblasts looks like the remaining tissue-building step.
reaction: Seeing the precursor processed outside the cells makes the sequence clearer.
reason: Combine the fibroblasts and matrix to complete the supporting tissue.
expectation: I expect a living supporting tissue containing fibroblasts and collagen-rich extracellular matrix.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch also needs work, but I want to finish the supporting tissue first.

effect: The supporting tissue goal is complete; the remaining goal is to prepare muscle-forming cells.
reaction: The cell–matrix attachments clarify that tissue is more than a bundle of collagen.
reason: The only offered combination advances the remaining muscle branch.
expectation: I expect the timed differentiation conditions to produce muscle progenitors or other muscle-forming cells.

effect: The muscle branch has produced committed individual cells with muscle-protein messages, but not mature muscle fibres.
reaction: The distinction between commitment and a mature fibre is clear.
reason: The only offered combination should use the messages to make muscle proteins and advance the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the cells to make muscle proteins from amino acids, though they may remain immature.

effect: The muscle branch produced separate, single-nucleus myoblasts rather than mature muscle fibres, completing the remaining goal.
reaction: The contrast between shared amino acids and different protein messages was useful, as was the distinction between myoblasts and mature fibres.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building living supporting tissue made the relationship between fibroblasts, secreted collagen and extracellular matrix concrete; the tissue was more than a collagen bundle.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final muscle-protein combination repeated the message-to-protein pattern already used for collagen, although the comparison served the chapter’s theme.

surprise.text: Procollagen was processed and assembled outside the cell before becoming part of the matrix, rather than emerging as finished collagen fibres.

arbitrary.text: Combining fibroblasts with matrix they had already produced felt a little artificial, though it had a clear purpose: showing their arrangement as living tissue.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how separate myoblasts develop into mature muscle fibres; the chapter leaves that process open.
